articles.title: Peterborough and Cambridge set for season-defining local derby
articles.summary: Peterborough United and Cambridge United are set for a potentially season-defining local derby at London Road.
articles.body:
Local derbies are always special, but none more so than when they have the ability to shape the narrative of a season. This much is true of Saturday's Cambridgeshire derby (12:30 GMT).

Robbie Savage's Peterborough United welcome Neil Harris' Cambridge United to London Road with both at something of a crossroads.

At stake for Posh? Their League One status. Despite an impressive win at Plymouth Argyle last time out, they remain 22nd in the table and need results to avoid a battle against the drop being the defining theme of their season.

As for the U's, the derby presents an opportunity to regain momentum. After October's 2-1 win at Barnsley they were one point off top spot, but failure to pick up three points in any of their five league games since leaves them caught between play-off contention and mid-table drift.

The derby also carries the weight of recent history, with the emotional baggage greater for the U's.

They have lost each of their past seven away league games against Peterborough, losing those matches by a combined 20-3 scoreline.

Indeed, they have not won at London Road since an FA Cup tie in 1994-95, while their wait for a league win at their rivals' home extends to 1990.

Savage, appointed last month, said his side were well aware of their responsibility for continuing that record.

"We don't want to be the group that loses to Cambridge at home, first time in 30 years I think it would be," he said.

"We don't want to be that group. We want to put three, four, five past them and win the game. Even if it's 1-0, it doesn't matter.

"It's all about winning, don't care we win, just win the game."

The victory at Plymouth ended a four-game wait for a win, and Savage said the onus was on his side to back it up on derby day. If they do, they know they will have secured successive league victories for the first time since February.

"This game is at the top of the mountain," he said.

"No doubt about it. The players will be up for it, we've shown them videos of the previous games, we've got fans sending messages.

"We're doing everything we can to make them realise how big this game is. It's not another game, it's the derby. A great game.

"Neil knows what it means. We're two passionate managers. He's done far better than me as a manager so far, so hats off to him. But we both want to win.

"They will bring 1,600 fans and we need to show Cambridge that we want to county to be blue."

While this derby is new territory for Savage, Harris comes armed with the memory of defeat in his only previous taste of the tie in a season than ultimately ended with relegation for the U's.

After securing a return to the third-tier in 2025-26 - and having made a competitive start to this campaign - there is no shortage of motivation to deliver a long-awaited win for his side.

"It is a one-off fixture," he told BBC Look East.

"There is a slightly different feel and mentality to it, but it means a hell of a lot to a hell of a lot of people.

"It means a lot to get bragging rights over a direct opponent. It's important to get back to our highest standards."

Posh have lost just one of their past 12 league games against Cambridge United, winning their past four in succession.

But with Savage's side in a precarious league position, there is optimism among fans that their 36-year long wait to celebrate a league win at London Road could finally arrive.

"It's about playing with heart and emotion, but brains as well," added Harris.

"We understand the importance of the fixture, I understand it as a driven manager. It's about trying to make sure we make our fans proud."

articles.title: "El Barcelona es más inseguro que el Madrid ahora mismo"
articles.standfirst: Los tertulianos de La Tribu analizan las debilidades de ambos equipos y la exigencia de la lucha por LaLiga
articles.summary: Los tertulianos de La Tribu analizan las debilidades de ambos equipos y la exigencia de la lucha por LaLiga
articles.body: Pablo Pinto, Nacho Labarga, Javi Lázaro, Luz Monzón, Pilar Losantos, Pepe Pasqués y han sido los tertulianos de este viernes en La Tribu, patrocinada por Sportium durante esta temporada, para analizar la actualidad deportiva marcada por el nivel de Barcelona y Real Madrid. Raúl Varela puso sobre la mesa una pregunta que generó el debate entre los tertulianos: ¿es más fácil ganar actualmente al Barcelona o al Real Madrid? Javi Amaro se decantó por el conjunto azulgrana: "Yo creo que si eres buen equipo es más fácil ganar al Barça". Nacho Labarga coincidió con Amaro y argumentó su postura a partir de las diferencias defensivas entre ambos conjuntos. "El Barça tiene más lagunas en defensa, tiene más problemas en defensa. El Madrid atrás está muy bien y además está jugando como un bloque", explicó. El periodista reconoció el potencial ofensivo del equipo de Flick, aunque incidió en sus problemas ante determinados rivales: "El Barcelona es un vendaval ofensivo, es un equipo que te puede matar y hacer siete goles, pero los grandes equipos a la contra le están pillando y en Europa le han pillado". Raúl Fuentes, sin embargo, recordó las dificultades que atravesó el conjunto blanco en su último compromiso europeo: "La primera parte del PSV, con todo el respeto, es de 1-4 si el PSV está acertado". Por su parte, Pilar Losantos reivindicó la importancia de la capacidad de reacción de los técnicos: "Parte de la gracia de los equipos es que tengan entrenadores con la personalidad suficiente como para que cuando ven el manifiesto desastre que hay tengan la capacidad para reaccionar y darle la vuelta". Javi Lázaro no encontró tantas diferencias entre ambos conjuntos. "Los dos tienen debilidades, a lo mejor no muchas, pero yo creo que los dos muestran debilidades de tanto en cuanto", señaló. El periodista puso el foco en la exigencia de la lucha por el campeonato liguero, incluyendo también al Atlético de Madrid. "Da la sensación de que ya el que se empieza a dejar puntos por el camino empieza a perder la Liga de verdad", afirmó. Lázaro recordó que hace unas semanas existía la sensación de que los grandes equipos podían fallar más durante esta temporada, algo que, a su juicio, no está sucediendo. "Aquí el que se deje puntos por el camino igual lo acaba pagando con un título menos", sentenció.

images.caption: Konaté, ante Hugo Álvarez en el último partido de Liga ante el Celta. CHEMA REY

articles.title: Mourinho: "El superordenador de la IA es una mierda"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador portugués atendió a la prensa antes del partido frente al Alavés en el Bernabéu
articles.summary: El entrenador portugués atendió a la prensa antes del partido frente al Alavés en el Bernabéu
articles.body: José Mourinho se subió a la palestra para hablar ante la prensa en la previa del partido frente al Alavés en el Bernabéu. El entrenador portugués habló de Vinicius, el estatus de Mbappé y Bellingham, el regreso de Mendy a una convocatoria... y terminó saludando a su primo periodista, presente en la sala de prensa, con el que aseguró que no puede hablar porque “se ha cambiado a un grupo que me trata muy mal”. Alavés: "Digo siempre que dos días entre partido es poco y tres días es bien... así que no vamos a tener ningún problema en recuperar a los jugadores tras el último partido. El Alavés está haciendo un gran trabajo y este año, la tranquilidad en la clasificación, nos espera otro partido complicado. Hay que jugar y sacar los tres puntos". Huijsen: "Defender bien también significa ayudar a ser mejor ofensivamente al equipo. Si tienes seguridad atrás, línea más alta y se ganan los duelos individuales... es parte del trabajo defensivo. Todo tiene consecuencias en el trabajo ofensivo. Dean cuando estaba conmigo en la Roma era un niño y todavía tenía un camino por recorrer. La dificultad de la Premier lo ha mejorado en muchas cosas... el año pasado no fue una buena temporada para él, pero el tiempo que estuvimos juntos lo ha ayudado a acelerar su crecimiento. Es todavía un niño, pero con mucha más madurez. Rüdiger es un jugador importante para él, el año pasado ya le ayudó y este también, como Konaté. Pasó bien la frustración de no ir al Mundial y ha sacado lo positivo. No demasiados halagos porque quizás luego le hace mal". Bellingham: "A mí no me gusta comparar futbolistas de diferentes generaciones. Zidane fue uno de los mejores de su generación y Jude ya es uno de los mejores de la suya". Vinicius: "Tengo dificultades de responder algunas de vuestras preguntas... porque yo no busco el once ideal, no existe. Hace semanas se tenía que marchar, luego que era incompatible con Diomandé... y ahora todo lo contrario. Las cosas no son tan lineales. Vini ha mejorado.. y que el grupo te quiera independientemente de su rendimiento es lo importante. Esa ha sido la base de Vinicius, esa estructura la han creado sus compañeros. En estos momentos ya está en ese nivel que nos ayuda... todo lo demás es secundario". Celebración de Diomande con Vinicius: "Es que no son competencia, estamos todos juntos y queremos todos lo mismo. Tenemos el mismo objetivo, no existe. Es una cosa que nos ha costado mucho construir y es de las cosas menos valoradas... pero es de las cosas más importantes. Que el equipo funcione como grupo. Estamos logrando una estabilidad y parece que vuestro objetivo es crear esta duda. No le interesa a nadie en el equipo". ¿Equipo sano?: "Caritas siempre encuentras, pero hasta ahora no he tenido ningún problema con el vestuario. Ha sido poco a poco, el periodo de pretemporada tienes ese tipo de situaciones. Son cinco meses juntos y no hemos tenido ningún problema. Si me llega, aquí estamos para ayudar... pero no creo. Veo a todos ellos con un mismo objetivo. La gente quiere jugar y a nadie le gusta estar fuera o no tener minutos. El objetivo colectivo van a superar las caritas del egoísmo individual". Líder después de 2 años complicados: "Me hace ilusión ganar al Alavés. Me gustaría ganar mañana... Para la Champions es muy pronto, no sabemos cómo vamos a llegar todos a los cruces. No quiero jugar la repesca, tenemos tantos partidos... Luego está la Supercopa, en principio dos partidos, también la Copa del Rey. Estamos cerca, con tres o cuatro puntos lo tenemos. La Champions son detalles. Mira el Bayern, que ha perdido a Kane, mira al PSG... Puedes llegar a los partidos decisivos sin jugadores importantes. Hay gente que dice que somos candidatos, luego está el súper ordenador de la IA... que es una mierda”. Elecciones en España: "No hay entrenamiento el domingo. No tenemos jugadores españoles (risas)... sólo tenemos tres o cuatro". Lesionados: "Mendy mañana va al banquillo. Y si va al banquillo, es que puede jugar. Tenemos tres laterales izquierdos, pero es muy buena noticia para todos que vuelva. Trent está fuera porque está enfermo. Y Rodrygo está en un momento bastante bueno, pero también está enfermo. Y a los enfermos los queremos lejos. Pero Rodrygo está trabajando mucho, ha cambiado el chip, me parecía un chico un poco adaptado a la lesión. Pero ahora está trabajando fuerte, no veo jugando contra el Arsenal ni jugando en Liga al final del año. Pero tiene una calidad increíble y será uno más de una plantilla increíble con jugadores extraordinarios". Escala de Vinicius en el equipo: "Es problema suyo, no mío. Mbappé y Bellingham están en la misma escala que todos. Si algún día van al banquillo... es lo que hay. El objetivo colectivo está por encima del individual. Entiendo tu pregunta, pero el hecho de que Kylian y Jude tengan tantos minutos y que solo hayan estado una vez en el banquillo (por Jude). La diferencia lo hace el rendimiento incomparable sobre el resto. Tenemos a Courtois que hace una diferencia increíble y por eso ha jugado todo menos un partido porque estaba enfermo. Y el que jugó por Courtois, Lunin, lo hizo perfecto y fue decisivo. Esta es la fuerza del equipo. Faltan dos meses antes del gran follón y no quiero a nadie para entrar y salir. No quiero noticias de mercado". Salir a tope desde el inicio: "Responsabilidad mía, obviamente. Pero ya hemos empezado partidos muy bien... que hemos terminado el partido en 30 minutos. Es un proceso esta perfección de empezar bien y terminar mejor. Llevamos aquí cinco meses y nos falta esta consistencia de empezar bien. He preguntado a un par de jugadores para tratar de entender las cosas y me han dado una respuesta muy graciosa... y me han dicho que si empiezan bien yo me aburro en el banquillo".

articles.title: Los nuevos se ponen las pilas
articles.standfirst: Gordon, Adeyemi y Gabriel Jesus, casi al mismo nivel que Lewandowski, Ferran y Rashford
articles.summary: Gordon, Adeyemi y Gabriel Jesus, casi al mismo nivel que Lewandowski, Ferran y Rashford
articles.body: Subidón de los nuevos en Bakú. El Barcelona goleó al Sabah (1-4) y lo hizo de la mano de sus tres caras nuevas en ataque. Anthony Gordon abrió el marcador en el 31' y repitió en el 51', tras un pase de Gabriel Jesus. Cuatro minutos después marcó Adeyemi, a pase de Balde, y en el 60' fue el brasileño el que vio puerta, aprovechando un rechazo del portero después de un cabezazo de Koundé. Es decir, los tres fichajes fabricaron todos los goles del Barça. Sin Lamine y Raphinha sobre el césped, dieron un paso al frente. Y de qué manera. Con esos cuatro tantos, el trío suma ya 15 goles en los 18 partidos oficiales que ha disputado el Barça esta temporada, entre LaLiga y la Champions. Gordon y Adeyemi llevan cinco cada uno en 17 encuentros, y Gabriel Jesus, otros cinco en solo 11. El brasileño es el que más rápido ve puerta y el que lleva mejor promedio porque anota un gol cada 47 minutos. Sin embargo, la comparación con el curso pasado todavía no les favorece. Se acercan, pero no llega. Lewandowski, Ferran Torres y Marcus Rashford marcaron entre los tres 54 goles en los 57 partidos oficiales del Barcelona en la temporada 2025-26. Ferran fue el más acertado, con 21 tantos en 49 partidos. Le siguió Lewandowski, con 19 en 46, y Rashford cerró la lista con 14 en 49. Los números hablan por sí solos. El trío de la pasada campaña promedió 0,95 goles por partido del equipo. El actual se queda en 0,83. Y si solo se cuentan LaLiga y la Champions, las dos competiciones que se han jugado hasta ahora este curso, la diferencia es todavía mayor. Lewandowski, Ferran y Rashford sumaron 50 goles en los 50 partidos que disputó el Barça en ellas. Gol por partido. La brecha está en LaLiga: los nuevos llevan siete goles en 13 jornadas, mientras que sus predecesores firmaron 38 en 38. En Europa, eso sí, la historia cambia. Gordon, Adeyemi y Jesus suman ocho goles en cinco partidos de Champions, por los 12 en 12 que marcaron Lewandowski, Ferran y Rashford. Ahí los nuevos fichajes ganan, y con claridad. Es cierto que la temporada no ha hecho más que empezar. Todavía no se han disputado ni la Copa ni la Supercopa, y los tres recién llegados necesitan tiempo para adaptarse a lo que les pide Flick. Lo van haciendo progresivamente, pero el Barça les exige más. Lo de Bakú fue un aviso de lo que pueden dar. Ahora les toca mantenerlo, y no solo ante uno de los rivales más flojos de la Champions. Faltan sus goles en partidos importantes.

images.caption: Gabriel Jesus, Adeyemi y Gordon celebran un gol en Bakú. GETTY IMAGES

articles.title: Southampton v Middlesbrough: Spygate revisited in Championship
articles.summary: Southampton and Middlesbrough prepare to re-ignite their rivalry as they meet for the first time since the Spygate scandal unfolded.
articles.body:
"I don't want to shut out the noise, we just need to know that it's coming and it's going to be electric."

The "noise" Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert refers to has been building over recent weeks, with 'Spygate' returning to the collective consciousness as Saints and Middlesbrough meet on Friday (20:00 GMT) for the first time since the scandal.

The most recent time they came face-to-face was in last season's Championship play-off semi-finals.

Saints ended up winning over the two legs, but were then expelled from the final having being caught spying on a Boro training session before the first match at the Riverside.

It turned into a five-month saga which started with a Saints performance analyst being photographed from behind a tree, and ended with Eckert being handed a suspended ban and fined £28,000.

The German head coach signed a new deal at Saints exactly a week ago and previously admitted the experience of Spygate had changed his life.

Now St Mary's awaits as the two sides will re-ignite their rivalry after a tough end to the last campaign for both.

Saints players felt aggrieved for not being allowed to feature in the play-off final, while Boro suffered the heartbreak of losing at Wembley, as Hull City won promotion to the Premier League.

"It's a massive game for both teams," former Nottingham Forest and Ipswich defender Luke Chambers told the 72+ podcast.

"Middlesbrough have bounced back tremendously well from the play-offs, the ups and downs, they didn't know if they were coming or going, and to go through that heartache of making the final and not getting over the line - credit to them.

"It will be an electric atmosphere and there will be added needle on the pitch, especially with some of the things that happened in the games between the two sides last season when the news broke out."

Hellberg reveals Eckert apology after Spygate

Southampton give head coach Eckert new deal

'It's changed my life' - Eckert on Spygate scandal

Hellberg and Eckert ready to move on - but can supporters?

Boro boss Kim Hellberg and Eckert both arrived at their respective clubs in November 2025 and have enjoyed plenty of success on the pitch over the past 12 months.

But following the 2-1 defeat in May's play-off semi-final second leg at St Mary's, Hellberg described it as "one of the toughest days" in his coaching career.

Although Friday's game promises to be filled with emotion on the pitch and in the stands, the two head coaches claim to have made up since the events of last season after Eckert called Hellberg to apologise over the summer.

"We spoke and he called me. I've always been a person who wants to give people a second chance," Hellberg told BBC Radio Tees.

"He has also gone though some things that have been very tough for him in terms of this which is something you don't wish anyone.

"I think in general for me it's overplayed. We have talked about it, everything has been sorted and now I'm looking forward to playing against a good side with a good manager and see how good we can be, and I'm really looking forward to it."

After Eckert took responsibility and apologised over the summer, both he and the club also expressed a desire to move on after the backing of the Saints board and owner Dragan Solak.

Some members of the Middlesbrough press have been robust and consistent in their strong criticism of Southampton and Eckert since Spygate first emerged.

Eckert had walked out of media conferences during the play-off semi-final following some stern questioning of him, while a piece was published on Thursday which questioned the German's character.

On Friday, Southampton published their own video , external on club channels, emotionally recalling the play-off campaign and how success was "ours... until it wasn't" before Boro "got another go", followed by footage of Oli McBurnie's winner for Hull at Wembley.

"People talk about last season, but we're focused on this one," narrates Southampton-based streamer Tyrone, over clips of goals from this season. "And now, here we are again; new hope, more reasons to believe, the same leader. We know all eyes are on us, and we're ready."

Southampton fan Rob Maddox echoed the emotions of both managers and felt that the majority of both fanbases want to now put the previous distaste behind them.

"There has been so much football since the play-off semi-final that I think both clubs are ready to get on with it now," he said.

"Some might look to hype the game up as a rivalry but I think the game should be looked at as two very good footballing sides going head to head.

"Of course there is going to be that little bit of spice and I'm sure we'll see it in the stands, but I hope that after the game we're talking about both teams showing off what they can do on the pitch."

Boro fan Jack McBride agreed that "Spygate's over and done with now" but admitted there was still a feeling of "bitterness" within the fanbases.

"I've seen some back and forth which is fun and all part of being a football fan, but there's also the other side of it which is bitter, twisted and they're still going on about it in a negative way," he told BBC Radio Tees.

"We had our chance and we didn't take it. Saints have had a four-point deduction, Tonda's been punished, we move on. Was it enough? Personally, I don't think that it was but we move on from it.

"This is a game we've all been looking to, and it was probably the first fixture that Boro and Saints fans were looking for.

"I think it's going to be quite a hostile atmosphere. I think Saints will be booing constantly and Boro fans will bring the noise as much as they can."

Hellberg reflects on 'fantastic year' at Boro

The sides' latest showdown is not only a tasty encounter because of the fallout from Spygate, but also because two of the division's best teams will be going toe-to-toe.

Boro are top of the table and have the Championship's leading goalscorer in Will Lankshear , who has scored 14 times in 15 appearances.

The 21-year-old joined the club from Tottenham Hotspur over the summer for a fee that could rise to as high as £20m, following an impressive loan spell at Oxford United.

Meanwhile, Saints forward Cyle Larin has also been enjoying something of a prolific campaign himself, netting eight times in his 13 matches.

Eckert's side are sixth, but would be fourth and three points off Boro if not for the four-point deduction handed to them because of Spygate.

The two sides have the best home records so far this season and have both scored more than 30 goals each across their 17 matches played.

"Friday's a massive game. A massive football game before anything else," Boro midfielder Myles Peart-Harris told BBC Radio Tees.

"The rivalry we now have is even better so the boys are looking forward to Friday. Hopefully we play our football, stick to what we know and get a result, we're ready.

"We're more excited about the game of football because we know they like to play football, we like to play football, so I think tactically it's going to be a great time for everyone to watch and most importantly we can go there and get a win."

Former Reading and Leyton Orient midfielder Jobi McAnuff told the 72+ podcast: "What it boils down to is two of the best teams in the league this year.

"I think it'll be a cracking atmosphere and there will still be needle there because it was such a huge story, it was massive.

"The implications and fallout went on for months and I think that will add to it. It will be a fantastic spectacle and I hope this season we are talking about what happens on the pitch rather than what's happened off it."

articles.title: European games marred by clashes as French President Emmanuel Macron condemns violence
articles.summary: Violent clashes mar a number of European football matches on Thursday night, with French president Emmanuel Macron condemning trouble at Marseille's home game against Levski Sofia.
articles.body:
Violent clashes marred a number of European football matches on Thursday night, with French President Emmanuel Macron condemning trouble at Marseille's home game against Levski Sofia.

There were also incidents at games between Turkish side Besiktas and Israel's Hapoel Be'er-Sheva in Georgia and Sunderland's 1-1 home draw with Poland's Jagiellonia Bialystok.

Uefa says it has appointed ethics and disciplinary inspectors "to conduct investigations into the incidents and examine all available evidence" from the Marseille-Levski Sofia and Besiktas-Hapoel Be'er-Sheva games.

European football's governing body said it "strongly condemns the serious incidents of violence and disorder" at those ties.

It added: "Violence, aggression, hatred and any form of provocative, discriminatory or extremist behaviour have no place in football.

"Uefa competitions are founded on the principles of respect, fair play, integrity and safety."

In Marseille, the build-up to the Europa League match at the Stade Velodrome was affected by incidents in the stands, including the throwing of projectiles and flares between the two sets of supporters.

With 10 minutes to go until kick-off, several Marseille fans ran from a home stand, appearing to pursue a group of Levski Sofia supporters.

They breached the stand designated for away fans, which housed around 500 supporters of the Bulgarian domestic champions.

"Five people were taken to hospital with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder," said the Marseille police prefecture. "Six others were treated on site for various wounds."

Macron spoke to Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev about the incidents, with the French president condemning "with the utmost force these acts of violence, which have no place in sport or in public space", and reassured him that "these acts would not go unpunished".

According to news agency Reuters, Radev thanked Macron for his personal involvement following the "attack on Bulgarian citizens" and for the medical assistance provided to the victims.

Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova said she found video footage of the incidents "shocking" in a statement posted on social media.

"The attacks against the Bulgarian fans desecrate one of the great games that brings millions of people together around the world," she added.

"Everyone should be able to support their team without being afraid for their safety."

Fan violence mars Marseille-Levski Sofia match

Police response to Besiktas fans' pro-Palestine banner 'unacceptable'

Sunderland held by Polish side Jagiellonia

Ligue 1 club Marseille said it was "working to understand the precise circumstances of these incidents".

The police source said all the people injured were Bulgarian and there was "no information at this stage regarding any arrests".

Security personnel managed to restore calm, allowing the game to kick-off on time, although there were a few further flare-ups between the fans, notably during the half-time break in a match Marseille won 1-0.

"It's a very regrettable episode. These are incidents which are unacceptable for football," said Levski Sofia coach Julio Velazquez

Marseille boss Bruno Genesio added: "We are living through violent times in our society, so this is very, very regrettable."

Meanwhile, the Turkish Football Federation has strongly condemned the "unacceptable" actions of Georgian police towards Besiktas fans who unfurled a pro-Palestinian banner during their Europa League match against Israeli side Hapoel Be'er-Sheva.

Besiktas say they have lodged a complaint with European football's governing body Uefa over "disproportionate" use of force by Georgian police.

The match had been moved from Istanbul to Batumi, Georgia for safety and security reasons but had to be suspended in the 25th minute after clashes involving Besiktas supporters and local police.

Both the officiating team and the Besiktas players left the field, but play was able to resume 30 minutes later.

"We strongly condemn the unacceptable attitudes, behaviour and actions directed at Besiktas supporters inside and outside the stadium before and during the Uefa Europa League match," said a statement from the Turkish federation.

Turkish outlet NTV reported that Georgian police had gone into the stands and used pepper spray on the Besiktas fans.

The report added that there were anti-Israeli chants from the Turkish fans and that Besiktas players and director of football Onder Ozen spoke to supporters to try to calm matters before play restarted.

Hakan Fidan, Turkey's minister of foreign affairs, spoke to his Georgian counterpart Maka Botchorishvili following the incident.

"All necessary steps are being taken to ensure the safety of our citizens and protect their rights," a Turkish foreign ministry source said.

At Sunderland, there were crowd disturbances after Jagiellonia Bialystok fans were found in areas of the Stadium of Light with home fans, despite Uefa having imposed an away supporter ban for the Europa League game.

Police and stewards attended some disruption early on during the match.

"In the build-up to the match, the club had put measures in place in line with this sanction and maintained regular communication with our supporters, Jagiellonia Bialystok and Uefa," said a Sunderland statement.

"Unfortunately, Jagiellonia Bialystok failed to engage and cooperate on this matter.

"We are disappointed that these measures and communications were disregarded by some visiting supporters and we will review the circumstances surrounding their entry into the stadium."

articles.title: EFL preview: Happy Potters and the deathly Hammers
articles.summary: BBC Sport explores five things to capture your attention this EFL weekend.
articles.body:
You've dug the de-icer and novelty jumpers out the back of the cupboard and within days a square of chocolate before breakfast will be socially acceptable again.

December is looming large, but you can be sure the season of goodwill does not extend to the English Football League.

There are furious battles raging at the top and bottom of the Championship, League One and League Two with more than a third of the campaign in the rear-view mirror and a huge month coming up which might just determine who will be on the naughty or nice list in 2027.

Here are five things to look out for across the EFL before the advent calendars are opened.

'Massive for both' - Saints and Boro revisit Spygate rivalry

If, as they say, seven days is a long time in football, then seven months feels like a lifetime.

In April, West Ham were trying to maintain a two-point cushion over Tottenham in the Premier League relegation scrap, while Stoke were careering down the Championship table. A run of one point from their final six matches saw them finish 17th.

On Saturday, they meet at the London Stadium (15:00 GMT) with the Potters 11 points and 11 places above the Hammers in this season's Championship standings.

Tuesday's defeat at Portsmouth means Scott Parker has taken just two points from four games since replacing Nuno Espirito Santo at the helm in east London, with his side now winless in six games.

The Hammers slipped into the bottom half of the table following Wednesday's results – the Irons have not finished lower than eighth in the second tier since 1956.

By contrast Mark Robins has led Stoke to five straight wins.

The 2-1 victory against Millwall on Wednesday means they have taken an incredible 35 points from their past 14 games, having begun the season with three straight losses.

A sixth win in a row might be enough to see Stoke take over at the top, given leaders Middlesbrough play at Southampton on Friday night, while a seventh game without a win could leave the Hammers closer to the relegation zone than the promotion places.

Unthinkable for the pre-season title favourites, and with six of their seven games before the turn of the year against sides scrapping for the automatic promotion spots or play-off places, this could just be the start of a bleak winter for the Irons.

As far as claret and blue teams freshly relegated from the Premier League go, West Ham have got it pretty good compared to Burnley.

Wednesday's 2-0 defeat by Birmingham at Turf Moor made it an English record 24 games without a home win, a run stretching back to October 2025.

Overall, the Clarets have won just one of their past 29 league games dating back to February - a 4-0 triumph at Watford on 10 October.

Fabio Celestini's side are second-bottom, a point above Derby, and could sink to the foot of the table if they fail to win at Millwall on Saturday (15:00 GMT).

Wednesday's 2-1 defeat at Stoke was a fourth straight defeat for Alex Neil's side who have taken just 12 points from their past 15 games, losing nine of them.

Pretty incredible seeing as how the Lions lost just 11 across the whole of last season, when they finished third, and might well have found themselves in the division above the Clarets this season, had things turned out differently in their play-off semi-final against Hull City.

Iordanescu starts at basement-dwellers Derby

The game at The Den is not the only intriguing one in the second tier this Saturday as new basement-boys Derby welcome crisis club Watford to Pride Park (15:00 GMT).

The Rams have taken two steps back after taking one forward, picking up their only win in their past 13 games when they beat Bolton at home on 6 November.

They lost 2-0 to Southampton last weekend and 3-0 at Wolves on Tuesday in a game where they allowed 39 shots on their goal - the most by any side in the Championship in 11 years.

Preston North End's resurgence has left the Rams bottom of the pile with 35 goals conceded in 17 matches - the worst in the second tier along with Burnley.

They welcome a Hornets side who are 20th, three points above the drop-zone, after Wednesday's 1-0 home defeat to Blackburn , before which the players met new boss Edward Iordanescu for the first time.

The Romanian certainly has a big task on his hands, Watford have taken a single point from eight away games and were thumped 4-0 at Sheffield United last Saturday in Alessio Dionisi's last stand, while they now haven't scored in three games overall.

Owls aim to get on a roll against Royals

We are going to find out an awful lot about Sheffield Wednesday's prospects in League One in the next three weeks.

Dave Challinor's arrival has seemingly steadied the ship, but a stalemate at Stevenage on Tuesday was a sideways step after back-to-back wins over Plymouth and Barnsley in which Wednesday rode their luck at times.

The Owls are fourth, five points off the top, and unbeaten in five, but have played a game more than most sides around them and face in-form promotion rivals Oxford United, Leicester and Luton in the run-up to Christmas after Saturday's visit of Reading (15:00 GMT).

The Royals have slipped to ninth after a run of one point from a possible 12, losing their past three and taking only six points from eight away games, with just one win.

They will be desperate to return to the play-off race and end their slump, and if they can do it the pressure will be firmly on Wednesday in the weeks to come.

Free-falling Millers seek to get out of the basement

In the past 14 seasons they have been promoted or relegated in 10 of them, but Millers fans will be keen for just a season of stability given the way things have started following the drop from League One last season.

An eight-match winless run has left Alex Bruce's Millers second-bottom, only off the foot of the EFL by virtue of scoring more than Crawley, level on points and goal difference - pretty incredible for a club which has spent more seasons in the Championship (seven) than anywhere else since they were last in the fourth tier in 2013.

They will seek to end their slide with Bruce sat in the stands on Saturday (15:00 GMT) when they host Oldham, a side who were mid-table in the National League when the Millers began their last Championship campaign, but now sit three points better off in 20th.

Rotherham actually picked up a creditable goalless draw at Grimsby last weekend, which denied the Mariners a place in the automatic promotion spots.

Fourth-placed Town will seek to put that right when they head to Crewe, two places behind on goal difference alone, this weekend, in a crazy division where just four points separate Grimsby from Fleetwood in 15th.

You can follow the entire EFL weekend as it happens here on the BBC Sport website and app, starting with live text coverage of Southampton v Middlesbrough on Friday, 27 November.

articles.title: Rubin Colwill: The local boy aiming to be at the heart of Cardiff City's derby aims
articles.summary: The Wales midfielder, central to Cardiff's change in fortunes, grew up in a Swansea-supporting area and has been the focal point of a Wales debate.
articles.body:
Rubin Colwill is used to being in the centre of things.

He has been the focus of an ongoing argument over his role - or lack of it - in Craig Bellamy's Wales side.

It has meant the midfielder has been the subject of countless questions around international weeks, the latest prompting the Wales boss to ask a journalist if he had a Colwill poster in the middle of his bedroom wall.

The debate has stemmed from the 24-year-old being at the heart of Brian Barry-Murphy's stylish transformation of Cardiff City.

So it is understandable that, as he prepares to lead his boyhood club into the eye of the storm that is the south Wales derby, he is again in the centre of things.

And fitting for someone who grew up in the middle of the rivalry between the two cities.

"I took a lot of stick," Colwill said. Well, we presume that is what he might have said, stopping himself from swearing to describe life as a Cardiff fan from the town of Neath, nine miles from Swansea.

"I probably felt it more than most being surrounded by Swansea fans and a lot of mates being Swansea fans.

"It was tough because they were in the Premier League for a long spell, so I was always trying to give a bit back when we won a game or did well."

Bellamy an influence as Williams leads Swansea

Bellamy jokes reporter has Colwill poster in bedroom

Latest Cardiff City news, analysis and fan views

Colwill was always Cardiff, as was brother Joel, his team-mate for club and country.

Their mother - from Port Talbot, a little further east with a denser amount of support that turn towards the capital - was a Cardiff fan and so were her boys, signing for the club while still in primary school.

He has never gone to a derby in Swansea as a fan - he was never allowed - but was part of the Cardiff side that last won at their rivals in 2021 and has told team-mates all about the journey down the M4, where fans flock to bridges and encouragement turns to abuse as the miles clock up.

He will mention that, and the feeling of the times where, by his own admission, Cardiff were not good enough in a string of defeats that sting more than most.

But he will also share the "no better" feeling of being in the middle of the celebrations of a derby win, as he was in January 2025.

That Cardiff 3-0 victory was a rare high point in a season that eventually saw the club relegated from the Championship and in desperate need of a rebuild.

They have done just that, transitioning into an eye-catching, exciting team, who - depsite failing to win away this season and going into the game on the back of a 4-0 defeat by Preston North End - are ready to show Swansea the Bluebirds are a different beast these days.

Colwill and his influence has been very much a central cog in that change.

He has been game time and responsibility by Barry-Murphy - including the armband that might not be obvious for such a seemingly laidback character.

The academy product says he has learned much from the journey, including a frustrating spell of injuries that have limited his impact to seven starts since the return to the Championship.

It has seemingly been noticed by Bellamy, who spoke before Wales' recent Nations League defeat to Portugal about how he has improved as a player.

"There has been a big change in his game," Bellamy said, a former academy coach of the talented midfielder.

"He is a player I really like watching - before I did and I didn't. Now I see a lot of good things."

Colwill responded with a man-of-the-match performance against Portugal in what was his first competitive Wales start in five years.

"It was almost like I got to experience my first game twice," smiled Colwill.

Bellamy - who has questioned Colwill's work off the ball - has said he felt able to be more "ruthless" with the youngster because of their long association.

"Everyone knows," said Bellamy of what he thought Colwill needed to do to improve. "And none more than him."

Williams to lead Swansea in south Wales derby

Frozen out Robinson told he has Cardiff future

Despite being in the middle of it all, Colwill has not changed in playing personality, and certainly showed no pressure when he reclaimed his Wales spot.

Clearly there is a resilience that goes beyond sticking with a Cardiff scarf in an area full of Swansea colours.

"I've tried to learn from those experiences and develop myself mentally and improve my resilience so I can almost take anything that comes my way," he says.

"I think that's a massive part of football: you've got to stay grounded, stay focused, regardless if you're doing really well or really badly because it's a massive part of the game to stay consistent in the end."

So what of the challenge to improve and being in the middle of the two different approaches to getting the most out of him?

"I think they're very similar," is Colwill's response. "They both want to control the game, the structure, the body shape, how they want us to play, the press and reaction to giving the ball away.

"In the fundamentals of the game, they're similar. Obviously they're both different people so the approaches to that are very different, and it's in the little details.

"With Craig, he's always had that approach of if he thinks you can offer something or improve on, it's on us to take it on board and be open to that constructive criticism.

"It's not always easy. I think he does have a high demand of you, but if you do make a change as he asks of you then he will play you."

After the stick, the carrot at Cardiff is the chance to follow in Bellamy's footsteps by scoring a winner in the derby at Swansea, as the Wales boss did in 2011 - Cardiff's last win there in front of travelling supporters.

Colwill smiles at the thought, just as he winces at the memories of the defeats - as a player and a fan - which is why he will not be telling team-mates to treat this game like just another.

"That attitude is almost like trying to protect yourself from the pressure," he argues. "But it's not. We have a lot of boys from the area who have come from the academy who really get the game and understand the whole picture of it and how important it is for everyone in the city.

"And we've got no fear of failure - if we lose we just leave it all out there, but we have full belief we can win."

If they do, it will come as no surprise if Colwill is at the heart of it.

articles.title: Edward Iordanescu: Takeaways from Watford manager's first interview
articles.summary: What we learned from new Watford manager Edward Iordanescu's first press conference.
articles.body:
New Watford boss Edward Iordanescu says he has inherited a "challenge" but also "an opportunity" as the club seeks to pull away from the Championship relegation zone.

The 48-year-old has replaced Alessio Dionisi, who was sacked on Sunday after only five months in charge, following a run of seven defeats in 10 league games.

Iordanescu became Watford's sixth new boss in less than 18 months and is the 25th manager since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012.

He will take charge of the Hornets for the first time on Saturday when they travel to bottom club Derby County.

The Romanian met the media for the first time on Friday, and set out his vision for his tenure.

The Watford job is Iordanescu's first since leaving Legia Warsaw in October 2025, having won the Polish Super Cup with them last season.

It is the 10th managerial post of his 15-year coaching career, which has taken in Bulgarian club CSKA Sofia as well as Steaua Bucharest and Cluj - who he guided to the Romanian title and two domestic cups after joining midway through the 2020-21 season.

He also spent two and a half years in charge of Romania, guiding them to the last 16 of Euro 2024, where they were beaten by the Netherlands.

However, in his first job in English football, he inherits a Watford side three points above the drop zone and facing a fight for their second-tier status.

"I'm proud more than anything else and I'm honoured and happy to be here, but I'm also very aware of the challenge in front of me," Iordanescu told BBC Three Counties Radio.

"I don't want to make promises. I know the fans are not happy in this moment, but also I know that my words are not enough to bring them back, so they wait for facts. We need that, but of course there is a lot of work to do, there is a process in front of us and I hope we make the next steps right away.

"For me it's a challenge but at the same time it's an opportunity and I want to transform this opportunity into something good for the club, for the fans. This is the most important [thing]."

Prior to the dismissal of Dionisi, former Watford player Tom Ince - who left the club at the end of the 2025-26 season - told the BBC's 72+ Podcast there was "so much control away from the manager" at Vicarage Road.

While Ince, now at League Two side Tranmere Rovers, added his respect of positives of chairman Gino Pozzo's practises, he is not alone in speaking out about the board's influence.

Former England boss Sam Allardyce stated he turned down the Watford job in 2019 after claiming he was told how the side should play and which players should be in the XI.

But Iordandescu revealed that is not his expectation.

"I know my borders and I know my responsibilities." he said. "I'm in this club with a lot of quality people, professionals, people that know, understand, in detail, football, but starting yesterday I'm the number one in the technical side.

"I don't believe there's somebody here in the club that can overcome the coach, taking the technical knowledge, so it will be my responsibility, but also the technical part will be my decision all the time."

Pioneer or coach-eater? The complex world of Pozzo's Watford

From a purely statistical perspective, Watford's laboured start to the season under Dionisi could be credited to one key deficiency.

The Hornets have scored the fewest goals in the Championship, with only 13 in their 17 matches so far.

However, Iordanescu said his primary objective was not to thrill, but to win.

He said: "I always prefer to win 1-0 than 4-2. One-nil means you have an organised team, a team with some responsibility to engage 100% and to give everything for the result.

"So for me the priority is not to score more goals - [it is] to start to be organised, to start to act and react together on the pitch, to start to understand that the mindset should be a little bit different than what it was until now and to start to be efficient.

"In time we will see about scoring more goals, definitely every coach wants the team to score as much as possible."

Iordanescu also appeared to confirm he was in talks about taking over while Dionisi was still in charge.

It was reported on 12 November that the Hertfordshire club were in talks with him, but Dionisi, who had only been appointed in June, remained in charge across the international break and for Saturday's 4-0 defeat at Sheffield United.

The Italian was sacked on Sunday, with Iordanescu appointed on Wednesday.

Iordanescu said he had "asked for time" from the Watford hierachy before accepting the role.

He said: "I wanted to understand very clearly the objectives, the targets, so when I gave the final response, I was aware of everything.

"I'm here, I'm enthusiastic, I'm positive, I'm confident we can do good things together, and the thing which I count most on is the potential of this very young team. One of the youngest teams in the league."

But Iordanescu also took time to pay tribute to his predecessor.

"He [Dionisi] definitely worked hard," said Iordanescu.

"He did and left good things, very good things, already I saw many of them. But in football when things don't run the way you want and when the results are not backing up your work, it's difficult.

"I know he is a coach that put a lot of heart in his work and thank him for the good things that he did, and also tried to achieve here."

The task at hand now for Iordanescu is to succeed where Dionisi, and so many other Hornets bosses since their Premier League relegation in 2022, could not.

articles.title: Sorloth condiciona el ataque... y el mercado
articles.standfirst: Más allá del 'roto' que deja en la delantera hasta enero, el Atlético también depende de su futuro para reforzarse con algo más que un lateral izquierdo. Sin ventas, difícil fichar
articles.summary: Más allá del 'roto' que deja en la delantera hasta enero, el Atlético también depende de su futuro para reforzarse con algo más que un lateral izquierdo. Sin ventas, difícil fichar
articles.body: Alexander Sorloth condiciona el futuro próximo del Atlético. En lo deportivo, por la lesión que deja a Simeone con sólo Julián Alvarez y Jonathan David como delanteros para afrontar los seis partidos que se vienen en un periodo de 23 días; en lo referente al mercado de fichajes, por tratarse de la llave con la que Mateu Alemany pueda manejarse con el músculo económico del que ahora mismo no dispone ante la evidente necesidad de reforzar la plantilla. Aunque haya tenido que esperar al 25 de noviembre para inaugurar su cuenta anotadora, la baja hasta enero de Sorloth deja al Atlético bajo mínimos en ataque y sin el único 9 puro, limitando así las variantes que su presencia ofrece al equipo cuando el partido pide balones en largo o juego aéreo en el área. Al mismo tiempo, también 'aparta' al noruego del escaparate desde el que podía buscar una salida que podría resultar beneficiosa para todas las partes. En este sentido, con Sorloth no siempre conforme con su volumen de minutos y, sobre todo, con un rol más próximo al de 'solución desde el banquillo' que al de titular indiscutible (de sus 115 presencias como rojiblanco ha salido de inicio en 50), su venta aparece como una posibilidad sobre la mesa desde hace varias semanas, tanto por el buen cartel que conserva en el fútbol europeo (la Juventus ya lo quiso en verano) como por el cambio de escenario desde el verano en el que el Atlético no contemplaba su salida de ningún modo. Cabe recordar que, entonces, al adiós de Griezmann se unía que el 'culebrón Julián' vivía su momento más álgido, que Jonathan David aún no había llegado como cedido (lo haría el último día) y que el Villarreal aún conservaba un 20% de un futuro traspaso (esa cláusula incluida en su fichaje durante el verano de 2024 tenía una vigencia de dos años). Condicionantes que ahora no impiden un cambio de aires de un Sorloth que además sigue sin confirmarse como el delantero en el que confiar las opciones de luchar por los títulos. Pero más allá de las dudas que despierta Sorloth prácticamente desde su llegada al Atlético, el estudio de una posible venta viene marcado también por las carencias existentes en la plantilla. Así, más allá de que sin el noruego sólo haya dos delanteros (obviamente su salida implicaría la llegada de otro atacante), la defensa pide a gritos refuerzos igualmente. En este sentido, Grimaldo no tiene recambio en el lateral izquierdo ni Llorente en el derecho salvo que se considerara a Pubill, pero en ese caso la nómina de centrales quedaría reducida a tres: Hancko, Le Normand y un Cuti Romero que, al mismo tiempo que ha representado un salto descomunal de nivel, ha dejado patente con su lesión la necesidad de más de seis efectivos atrás Una necesidad detectada tanto por el cuerpo técnico (Simeone no ha ocultado que necesita refuerzos) como por un propio Mateu Alemany, si bien el problema es la falta de liquidez. Decidido desde hace semanas que el remanente del verano iba a destinarse a un lateral zurdo (estaba todo acordado el 1 de septiembre con Tagliafico y el Olympique de Lyon y en el último momento se desechó), el resto de incorporaciones quedan prácticamente ligadas a una venta. De ahí que, aunque esté prevista la cesión de Obed Vargas y haya jugadores como Arnau Ortiz con el futuro a estudiar, todas las miradas se dirijan a Sorloth.

articles.title: Maresca: "Haaland no está contento"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del City habla del momento de su delantero estrella
articles.summary: El técnico del City habla del momento de su delantero estrella
articles.body: Enzo Maresca, técnico del Manchester City, confirmó que Erling Haaland no está contento con el momento que atraviesa el club, inmerso en una mala racha de resultados y con el fantasma de las sanciones por las irregularidades financieras que amenaza a los 'Sky Blues'. El delantero noruego, que no ha visto puerta en ninguno de los últimos tres partidos del equipo, pese a disputar los noventa minutos en todos ellos, mostró su malestar después de que el City sumara el cuarto encuentro consecutivo sin ganar al empatar este martes contra el Nápoles. "Erling es un ganador. Es normal que no esté contento porque no ganamos partidos, pero no es solo Erling, es todo el mundo. Solo hace unas semanas estaba jugando genial. Ahora está triste y yo estoy triste porque no ganamos partidos, pero este es nuestro trabajo. Esto es el fútbol", dijo Maresca este viernes en rueda de prensa. El técnico italiano también fue cuestionado por los gestos de frustración del delantero sobre el campo. "Creo que también gesticular cuando ganamos partidos y no le llega la pelota. Es un delantero y vive del gol y de ganar partidos. Si no marcan o si no ganan, están tristes. Seguro que no está contento, pero todos estamos igual". Maresca también comentó que Haaland se está entrenando con normalidad y que no ve ningún problema con el delantero noruego, que tiene contrato con el City hasta 2034.

articles.title: Floro, Butragueño y José Luis Zalazar, en la despedida de Rafael Candel
articles.standfirst: El ex presidente del mítico Queso Mecánico fue enterrado en Albacete
articles.summary: El ex presidente del mítico Queso Mecánico fue enterrado en Albacete
articles.body: Personalidades del mundo del fútbol y del deporte han despedido este viernes al expresidente del Albacete, Rafael Candel, que estuvo al frente del club manchego en dos etapas, especialmente recordada la primera, entre 1988 y 1993, cuando logró que el club blanco ascendiese a Primera división. En su funeral, celebrado en la catedral de Albacete, estuvieron presentes Benito Floro, entrenador del 'Queso Mecánico' que tan famoso se hizo en la década de los 90; y Emilio Butragueño, exjugador del Real Madrid y actualmente director de Relaciones Institucionales de la entidad madrileña. También acudió el actual consejero delegado del club, Víctor Varela, y otros nombres muy ligados a la entidad manchega como el entrenador Julián Rubio; el exentrenador de las categorías inferiores de la selección española que salió del Albacete, Ginés Meléndez; o Pepe Carcelén, segundo entrenador junto a José Antonio Camacho en distintos equipos. Asimismo acudieron exfutbolistas como Antonio Catali o el uruguayo José Luis Zalazar, quien para muchos es el mejor jugador de la historia blanca, y que declaró que tiene "multitud de anécdotas con Candel", a la vez que destacó su "lado muy humano" y lo que ayudaba a todos "para crecer". En la misma línea se manifestó Julián Rubio, quien dijo estar "emocionado" ante el adiós del que ha dicho era su "amigo" y una persona con la que empezó en el banquillo y que "siempre estaba para ayudar al Albacete Balompié".

articles.title: El problema del Madrid con Nico Paz: "Su deseo choca con la realidad y la Premier ya ha preguntado por él"
articles.standfirst: Matteo Moretto desvela que el Manchester United ha preguntado por la situación del argentino, cuyo deseo es regresar al Bernabéu
articles.summary: Matteo Moretto desvela que el Manchester United ha preguntado por la situación del argentino, cuyo deseo es regresar al Bernabéu
articles.body: El futuro de Nico Paz empieza a entrar en una fase decisiva. El Real Madrid tiene la posibilidad de recuperar al futbolista argentino, cuyo deseo de regresar al Santiago Bernabéu ha quedado patente en varias ocasiones. Sin embargo, entre lo que quiere el jugador y lo que puede ofrecerle actualmente el conjunto blanco existe una diferencia importante. Y ahí es donde pueden aparecer otros pretendientes. Matteo Moretto ha explicado en 'Despierta San Francisco', junto a David Sánchez, cuál es la situación del centrocampista y ha dejado una reflexión que puede marcar el desenlace de la operación: "Yo creo que aquí su deseo choca un poco con la realidad". El periodista italiano pide paciencia porque, de momento, no hay una decisión definitiva: "Primero, hay que esperar un poco porque aún no se ha tomado ninguna decisión ni por parte del Madrid ni por parte del futbolista. El chico está súper centrado en el cómo". El deseo de Nico Paz, en cualquier caso, no ofrece demasiadas dudas. "El chico mismo ha dicho varias veces que su deseo sería volver a jugar para el Real Madrid", explica Moretto. Pero ese regreso tiene una condición fundamental: el protagonismo. El argentino quiere dar un paso adelante en su carrera y no contempla volver al Bernabéu para tener un papel testimonial. "Porque a nivel deportivo, Nico quiere ser protagonista. Nico quiere jugar", insiste el periodista. Una exigencia que puede chocar con la realidad de la plantilla madridista. De hecho, Moretto es bastante contundente al analizar el escenario actual: "La verdad es que de momento no hay sitio para Nico en ese Real Madrid". Y mientras el Real Madrid valora qué hacer con uno de sus talentos, desde Inglaterra empiezan a moverse. El futuro de Nico Paz también despierta interés en la Premier League, donde varios clubes han querido conocer de primera mano cuál es su situación. Moretto pone el foco especialmente en el Manchester United y confirma los primeros contactos para conocer el escenario del futbolista: "Te confirmo que hay clubes de la Premier que han preguntado a su entorno qué tal la situación. Sobre todo el Manchester United". Una información que añade un nuevo ingrediente a la operación. El conjunto inglés sigue pendiente de Nico Paz y ya ha buscado información sobre su futuro. El periodista también hace referencia a la conexión de Pochettino con el futbolista a través de su representante: "Pochettino comparte representante con Nico Paz. Y sí, es cierto que preguntaron por él". No obstante, conviene no precipitar acontecimientos. Moretto no habla de una oferta formal ni de negociaciones avanzadas, sino de un interés que empieza a tomar forma mientras el argentino decide qué camino quiere seguir. El Real Madrid tiene una cuestión importante que resolver. Según explica Moretto, el club blanco puede recuperar a Nico Paz a final de temporada por 80 millones de euros, aunque advierte de que existe también un componente estratégico relacionado con los derechos del jugador. "El Madrid a final de temporada puede repescarle por 80 kilos simplemente para este final de temporada. Porque si no, luego va a perder los derechos de Nico Paz", señala el periodista. La operación, por tanto, no depende únicamente de que el Real Madrid quiera recuperar al futbolista. También habrá que conocer qué papel le ofrece y si ese escenario convence a Nico. El argentino tiene claro que quiere jugar y ser importante, algo que puede abrir la puerta a otros proyectos si no encuentra esas garantías en el Bernabéu. Por ahora, toca esperar. Moretto considera que el jugador no tiene prisa por tomar una decisión y que el asunto todavía necesitará tiempo: "Yo creo que Nico esperará. Esta decisión se va a alargar un poco". ¿Hasta cuándo? El periodista italiano apunta directamente al calendario y marca una fecha aproximada para empezar a despejar las incógnitas: "Yo creo que hay que esperar hasta abril más o menos". El deseo de Nico Paz es volver al Real Madrid, pero el Manchester United ya ha preguntado por él y la falta de espacio en la plantilla blanca puede cambiar el escenario. El Bernabéu sigue siendo su sueño, aunque el argentino tiene una prioridad que está por encima de cualquier escudo: jugar. Y esa puede ser la clave de todo.

articles.title: Journalist: Liverpool closing in on agreement with midfielder

articles.body:
Liverpool Closing in on New Trey Nyoni Contract as Lewis Steele Shares Update

Liverpool could be moving closer to securing the long-term future of Trey Nyoni, with journalist Lewis Steele suggesting that a new contract for the talented midfielder could be agreed within the next few weeks.

Speaking to Dave Davis on Anfield Index's Media Matters podcast, Steele discussed Nyoni's impressive development, his performances under Andoni Iraola and the importance of Liverpool securing his future.

The 19-year-old impressed during Liverpool's Champions League victory over Club Brugge, with his maturity in possession and ability to dictate play earning considerable praise from both contributors.

Perhaps most encouraging for Liverpool supporters was Steele's revelation regarding the presence of Nyoni's representatives in Belgium and his understanding of the midfielder's contract situation.

Trey Nyoni Contract Update Offers Encouragement for Liverpool

Steele revealed that Nyoni's family and agent were sitting close to him during Liverpool's European victory in Belgium, before discussing the possibility of an imminent contract agreement.

"His family was sat near me the other night. His agent was sat near me," revealed Steele.

"Maybe a new deal is on the horizon soon."

The journalist then offered further encouragement regarding the progress of negotiations and the potential timeframe for an agreement.

"I think he's been offered one. So if that one gets done in the next couple of weeks, wouldn't be surprised at all."

Steele's understanding suggests that Liverpool have already taken steps towards securing Nyoni's future, with a contract offer seemingly on the table.

Davis was equally enthusiastic about the prospect of the midfielder extending his stay at Anfield.

"That is a player you want to get tied down long term," said the podcast host.

Trey Nyoni Impressing With Maturity Beyond His Years

Much of the conversation focused on Nyoni's performances and the remarkable composure he demonstrates at such a young age.

Davis highlighted an impressive statistic from Opta, revealing that Nyoni is averaging 26.4 forward passes per 90 minutes across all competitions this season, the highest figure among midfielders who have played at least 90 minutes for Premier League clubs.

Steele believes that willingness to progress possession is among the midfielder's greatest qualities.

"He's a really good midfielder to watch," explained Steele, highlighting how Nyoni is always looking to progress the play and set the tempo.

"The best thing you can say is he is only 19."

Steele went on to suggest that Nyoni has the appearance of someone who has already spent a decade playing in midfield, before discussing the possibility of him occupying that position at Liverpool for the next ten years.

Having interviewed Nyoni on several occasions, Steele also offered an interesting observation regarding the youngster's maturity.

"When you watch him in possession, he plays with a maturity that is way beyond what you'd expect of a 19-year-old."

Liverpool Recognise Importance of Securing Nyoni's Future

Nyoni's emergence also featured in the wider discussion regarding Liverpool's midfield recruitment plans.

Steele acknowledged that the resurgence of Alexis Mac Allister and Nyoni's development have eased some of his previous concerns surrounding Liverpool's midfield options.

The journalist also referenced Nyoni when discussing Liverpool's ability to demonstrate a pathway into senior football to prospective young signings.

"They can say, well, look at what we've done with these players," explained Steele, discussing Nyoni and Rio Ngumoha.

Securing Nyoni's future would clearly be welcomed by both podcast contributors, with Steele particularly enthusiastic about the teenager's potential.

"He's got a massive, massive future and now it's on Liverpool to tie him down to that new deal."

Confirmation of a contract agreement remains outstanding, although Steele's suggestion that an offer has already been made provides encouragement that Liverpool could secure Nyoni's future relatively soon.

articles.title: Official: Another Real Madrid star signs new contract
articles.summary: La Liga giants Real Madrid have this week announced the latest important contract extension in the club’s first-team ranks. This comes amid confirmation of B...
articles.body:
La Liga giants Real Madrid have this week announced the latest important contract extension in the club's first-team ranks. This comes amid confirmation of Brahim Díaz committing his long-term future to Los Blancos.

The subject of contract renewals has of course dominated the headlines in Spain's capital over the last couple of weeks.

As the Bernabéu brass work towards securing the club's long-term future, all of Aurélien Tchouaméni, Arda Güler and Thibaut Courtois have put pen to paper on fresh terms.

And as alluded to above, on Friday, yet another member of José Mourinho's squad has followed suit.

Brahim Díaz has endured something of a challenging campaign to date at Real Madrid, with just a pair of starts to his name between La Liga and the Champions League.

But the Moroccan's trust in his role moving forward has evidently not been shaken as a result. As per a statement across Los Merengues' website and social media channels:

'Real Madrid C. F. and Brahim Díaz have agreed to extend the contract of our player, linking him to the club until June 30, 2031.'

articles.title: Florida State vs. Florida: Uniform combinations revealed
articles.summary: The Florida State Seminoles have announced their uniform combination for their game against the Florida Gators.
articles.body:
The Florida State Seminoles play the Florida Gators at Doak, and are looking to get a win to secure bowl eligibility and a win over the Gators for the first time since 2023.

In their last meeting, Florida defeated FSU, 40-21. FSU has a 27-38-2 record against the Gators in their lifetime, with matchups dating back to 1958. In their last 10 meetings, the Gators and Seminoles have split the series, 5-5.

For 2026's game, Florida State will be going with a gold helmet, garnet jersey, gold pants, and garnet shoes. FSU has worn these jerseys since the 2023 season , when they partnered with Nike to create their Vapor F.U.S.E. look.

Kickoff for today's game between FSU and Florida is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. ET. Fans can catch the action on ABC.

Contact/Follow us @FSUWire on X, and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of FSU news, notes, and opinions. Jacob Smith is a contributor for FSU Wire, part of the USA TODAY Network. You can also follow Jacob on X at @jsmith_sports .
